Inline HTML in your Markdown now renders. More at [www.malgel.com](https://www.malgel.com).

## New

- **Inline HTML tags render as they would in a browser:**
  - `<small>` for smaller text, `<sub>` and `<sup>` for H₂O and x², and `<kbd>` for keys like <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>S</kbd>.
  - `<mark>` to highlight, `<ins>` to underline, `<code>`, `<cite>` and `<q>`.
  - `<abbr title="…">`, which shows its title when you hover over it.
  - Text colored with `<span style="color: …">` or `<font color="…">`. Named colors follow your theme.
- **Exports keep them too.** HTML export now passes these tags through (with their `class`, for your own style sheet) instead of showing them as text, and PDF and Word exports format them to match the preview.

Other tags are still left out, keeping the text inside them.

## Downloads

| System | File |
| --- | --- |
| macOS 11+ (Apple silicon and Intel) | `Malgel-0.1.2-macos-universal.dmg`: open it and drag Malgel to Applications |
| Windows 10+ | `Malgel-0.1.2-windows-x64-setup.exe` (installer) or `Malgel-0.1.2-windows-x64.zip` (portable) |
| Linux x86_64 | `Malgel-0.1.2-x86_64.AppImage` (`chmod +x` it, then run it) or `malgel-0.1.2-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` |

The macOS app is signed and notarized. The Windows files aren't signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may warn the first time: choose **More info → Run anyway**. `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists every file's checksum.
